# Milestone brief — ui-uplift-m7

**Title:** Author a two-voice type scale
**Kind:** milestone
**Roadmap:** ui-uplift (plans/ui-uplift/roadmap.yaml)
**Status:** planned
**Lane:** now
**Target:** 2026-08-11 -> 2026-08-22

## Parent epic

- ui-uplift-e1 — Material and type foundation — the D-1 Ledger Sheet core
  Replace the stitched two-source palette (a self-documented GitHub-Primer dark clone plus an unattributed bespoke light block) with one authored OKLCH family; author the product's first real type scale and its first letter-spacing; then retire .card as a primitive in favour of a graded hairline rule ladder. These three are the signature direction and they are strictly ordered — the rule ladder cannot ship before the material, because rules become the sole structural device and the light border token is 1.342:1 today.

## Summary

UPL-3. Meta 11px uppercase tracked +0.06em, small 13px, body 16px, section 20px, title on a clamp; sans for prose, --mono for every id, path, slug, timestamp, corpus version and state token. Introduces the first letter-spacing declaration in the product's history. Both voices are system stacks — zero font files, zero bytes, zero CSP impact. Highest value-to-cost ratio in the catalog and INDEPENDENT of the material milestone, so it can run in parallel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given the heading scale, when measured, then the h2-to-body step is no longer 1.10x and hierarchy is not carried by font-weight alone
2. Given any identifier surface (paper id, slug, path, timestamp, corpus version, state token), when rendered, then it uses --mono and inherits the existing tabular-nums scope
3. Given a 390px viewport, when the page title renders, then it scales via clamp() rather than staying fixed at 32px
4. Given the type tokens, then they extend the existing :root block and do not parallel-define a second token set
